swish: (transitive, slang, dated) To flog; to lash.
swiss: Of, from, or pertaining to Switzerland or the Swiss people.

switch: A device to turn electric current on and off or direct its flow.
(rail transport, US, Philippines) A movable section of railroad track which allows the train to be directed down one of two destination tracks; (set of) points.
switchboard: (telecommunications) The electronic panel that is used to direct telephone calls to the desired recipient.

swordsmanship: the skill of using a sword
swot: (intransitive, slang, UK, Irish, Commonwealth) To study with effort or determination.
sycamine: A tree, mentioned in Luke's Gospel, and thought to be the black mulberry.

syllable: (linguistics) A unit of human speech which often forms words corresponding to one opening of the mouth; a vowel and its surrounding consonants.

symbiosis: A relationship of mutual benefit, especially among different species.
symbiotic: (ecology) Of, or relating to symbiosis; living together.
symbol: A character or glyph representing an idea, concept or object.
symbolism: Representation of a concept through symbols or underlying meanings of objects or qualities. [from between 1645 and 1655.]
symbolize: (transitive) To be symbolic of; to represent.
symmetry: Exact correspondence on either side of a dividing line, plane, center or axis.
sympathy: A feeling of pity or sorrow for the suffering or distress of another.
The ability to share the feelings of another.
symphony: An extended piece of music of sophisticated structure, usually for orchestra.

synchronization: The state or property of being synchronized.
syncopation: (music) The quality of a rhythm being somehow unexpected, in that it deviates from the strict succession of regularly spaced strong and weak beats in a meter.

syndicate: (crime) A group of gangsters engaged in organized crime.

syntax: A set of rules that govern how words are combined to form phrases and sentences.

syrup: Any thick liquid that has a high sugar content and which is added to or poured over food as a flavoring.

systematics: The classification system of a branch of science, especially the classification of organisms in biology.

séance: A ceremony where people try to communicate with the spirits of dead people, usually led by a medium.
sōma: A city in Fukushima Prefecture, Japan.
